body.text:
There are two numbering systems for this text. The material is
sometimes organized into twelve themes and numbered accordingly.
Those numbers are given in brackets. The editions used were:
- Stava-kalpa-druma, (ed.) Bhakti Saranga Goswami. Vrindavan, 1959
- śrī-śrī-caitanya-candrāmṛta, (ed.) Bhakti Vilasa Tirtha. Mayapur,
  Chaitanya Math. 3rd edition, 1992.
Texts without an alternative number are not found in either one of
the editions. No attempt has been made to provide alternative readings.

The editions used were: - Stava-kalpa-druma, (ed.) Bhakti Saranga Goswami. Vrindavan, 1959 - śrī-śrī-caitanya-candrāmṛta, (ed.) Bhakti Vilasa Tirtha. Mayapur, Chaitanya Math. 3rd edition, 1992. body.text:
stumas taṃ caitanyākṛtim ativimaryāda-paramā-
dbhutaudāryaṃ varyaṃ vraja-pati-kumāraṃ rasayitum |
viśuddha-sva-premonmada-madhura-pīyuṣa-laharīṃ
pradātuṃ cānyebhyaḥ para-pada-navadvīpa-prakaṭam ||1|| (1)
body.translated_text: We praise Him who has the form of <s>Caitanya</s>, whose supremely extraordinary generosity transcends all limits, the best among all, who manifested in <s>Navadvīpa</s>, the supreme abode, to relish the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, and to bestow upon others the wave of sweet nectar of pure divine love-intoxication. ||1|| (1)

body.text:
sarvair āmnāya-cūḍāmaṇibhir api na saṃlakṣyate yat svarūpaṃ
śrīśa-brahmādy-agamyā sumadhura-padavī kāpi yasyāsti ramyā |
yenākasymāj jagac-chrī-hari-rasa-madirā-mattam etad vyadhāyi
śrīmac-caitanya-candraḥ sa kim u mama girāṃ gocaraś cetaso vā ||2|| (137)
body.translated_text: Whose true form is not perceived even by all the crest-jewels of the <s>Āmnāyas</s> (Vedas), who possesses a certain sweet path inaccessible even to <s>Śrīśa</s> (the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>) and <s>Brahmā</s>, by whom this world was suddenly made intoxicated with the wine of the <s>rasa</s> of <s>Śrī Hari</s> — can that <s>Śrīmac-Caitanya-candra</s> possibly be within the range of my words or my mind? ||2|| (137)

body.text:
dharme niṣṭhāṃ dadhad anupamāṃ viṣṇu-bhaktiṃ gariṣṭhāṃ
saṃbibhrāṇo dadhad ahaha hṛt-tiṣṭhatīvāśma-sāram |
nīco goghrād api jagad aho plāvayaty aśru-pūraiḥ
ko vā jānāty ahaha gahanaṃ heama-gaurāṅga-raṅgam ||3|| (127)
body.translated_text: Maintaining unparalleled steadfastness in <s>dharma</s>, bearing the most exalted devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, yet having a heart as if made of stone — alas! One lower even than a cow-killer floods the world with streams of tears — who indeed can fathom the profound play of the golden-limbed one (<s>Hema-gaurāṅga</s>)? ||3|| (127)

body.text:
dharmāspṛṣṭaḥ satata-paramāviṣṭa evātyadharme
dṛṣṭiṃ prāpto na hi khalu satāṃ sṛṣṭiṣu kvāpi no san |
yad datta-śrī-hari-rasa-sudhā-svāda-mattaḥ pranṛtya-
ty uccair gāyaty atha viluṭhati staumi taṃ kañcid īśam ||4|| (2)
body.translated_text: Untouched by <s>dharma</s>, constantly supremely possessed by irreligion, never having gained the sight of the virtuous, not existing anywhere in creation — yet intoxicated by tasting the nectar of <s>Śrī Hari's</s> <s>rasa</s> bestowed by Him, he dances wildly, sings aloud, and rolls on the ground — I praise that certain Lord. ||4|| (2)

body.text:
akasmād evāvirbhavati bhagavan-nāma-laharī
parītānāṃ pāpair api purubhir eṣāṃ tanu-bhṛtām |
aho vajra-prāyaṃ hṛd api navanītāyitam abhūn
nṝṇāṃ yasmin loke'vatarati sa gauro mama gatiḥ ||5|| (110)
body.translated_text: Suddenly the wave of the Lord's name manifests for these embodied beings even though they are surrounded by many sins — alas, even hearts hard as thunderbolts become soft as butter — He in whose descent into the world this occurs, that golden one (<s>Gaura</s>) is my refuge. ||5|| (110)

body.text:
na yogo na dhyānaṃ na ca japa-tapas-tyāga-niyamā
na vedā nācāraḥ kva nu bata niṣiddhādy-uparatiḥ |
akasmāc caitanye'vatarati dayāsāra-hṛdaye
pumarthānāṃ mauliṃ param iha mudā luṇṭhati janaḥ ||6|| (111)
body.translated_text: Neither <s>yoga</s> nor <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), nor chanting, austerity, renunciation, or observances, neither the <s>Vedas</s> nor proper conduct — where indeed is cessation of prohibited acts? Yet when <s>Caitanya</s>, whose heart is the essence of compassion, descends, people here joyfully plunder the crown jewel of all human goals (<s>puruṣārthas</s>). ||6|| (111)

body.text:
yan nāptaṃ karma-niṣṭhair na ca samadhigataṃ yat tapo-dhyāna-yogai-
rvairāgyais tyāga-tattva-stutibhir api na yat tarkitaṃ cāpi kaiścit |
govinda-prema-bhājām api na ca kalitaṃ yad-rahasyaṃ svayaṃ tan-
nāmnaiva prādurāsīd avatarati pare yatra taṃ naumi gauram ||7|| (3)
body.translated_text: What was not attained by those devoted to ritual action, nor realized through austerity, meditation, or <s>yoga</s>, nor by renunciation, the essence of truth, or hymns of praise, nor conceived by any through logic, and the secret of which was not fathomed even by devotees of <s>Govinda's</s> love — that very thing manifested of its own accord through the Name alone, where the Supreme descended — I bow to that <s>Gaura</s>. ||7|| (3)

body.text:
dhig astu brahmāhaṃ vadana-pariphullān jaḍa-matīn
kriyāsaktān dhig dhig vikaḍa-tapaso dhik ca yaminaḥ |
kim etān śocāmo viṣaya-rasa-mattān nara-paśūn
na keṣāṃcil leśo'py ahaha milito gaura-madhunaḥ ||8|| (32)
body.translated_text: Fie upon those dull-witted ones whose faces bloom with "I am <s>Brahman</s>," fie, fie upon those attached to rituals, fie upon those of harsh austerities, and fie upon the ascetics! Why should we lament over these human animals intoxicated with the taste of sense objects — not even a trace, alas, of the honey of <s>Gaura</s> has reached any of them! ||8|| (32)

body.text:
badhnan prema-bhara-prakampita-karo granthīn kaṭī-ḍorakaiḥ
saṅkhyātuṃ nija-loka-maṅgala-hare-kṛṣṇeti-nāmnāṃ japan |
aśru-snāta-mukhaḥ svam eva hi jagannāthaṃ didṛkṣur gatā-
yātair gaura-tanur vilocana-mudaṃ tanvan hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||9|| (16)
body.translated_text: Tying knots on his waist-cord with hands trembling from the weight of divine love (<s>prema</s>), chanting the names of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who removes the inauspiciousness of His own devotees while counting them, his face bathed in tears, desiring to see his own Lord <s>Jagannātha</s> — may that <s>Hari</s> of golden body, who bestows delight to the eyes of those who have come and gone, protect you! ||9|| (16)

body.text:
pāṣāṇaḥ pariṣocito'mṛta-rasair naivāṅkuraḥ sambhavet
lāṅgūlaṃ saramāpater vivṛṇataḥ syād asya naivārjavam |
hastāv unnayatā budhāḥ katham aho dhāryaṃ vidhor maṇḍalaṃ
sarvaṃ sādhanam astu gaura-karuṇābhāve na bhāvotsavaḥ ||10|| (36)
body.translated_text: Even if a stone is sprinkled with nectar, no sprout will emerge; even if one straightens the tail of a dog, it will never be straight; how can the wise, raising their hands, hold the orb of the moon? Without the compassion of <s>Gaura</s>, all spiritual practice may be there, but there will be no festival of divine love (<s>bhāvotsava</s>). ||10|| (36)

body.text:
saundarye kāma-koṭiḥ sakala-jana-samāhlādane candra-koṭir
vātsalye mātṛ-koṭis tridaśa-viṭapito'py adbhutaudārya-koṭiḥ |
gāmbhīrye'mbhodhi-koṭir madhuramaṇi sudhā-kṣīra-mādhvīka-koṭir
gauro devaḥ sa jīyān praṇaya-rasa-pade darśitāś carya-koṭiḥ ||11|| (101)
body.translated_text: In beauty, equal to millions of <s>Kāmadevas</s>; in delighting all people, equal to millions of moons; in parental affection, equal to millions of mothers; in wondrous generosity, surpassing even the divine wish-fulfilling tree by millions; in depth, equal to millions of oceans; in sweetness, equal to millions of nectars, milk-oceans, and honey — may that Lord <s>Gaura</s>, who has displayed wonders of millions in the domain of loving <s>rasa</s>, be ever victorious! ||11|| (101)

body.text:
premā nāmādbhutārthaḥ śravaṇa-patha-gataḥ kasya nāmnāṃ mahimnaḥ
ko vettā kasya vṛndāvana-vipina-mahā-mādhurīṣu praveśaḥ |
ko vā jānāti rādhāṃ parama-rasa-camatkāra-mādhurya-sīmām
ekaś caitanya-candraḥ parama-karuṇayā sarvam āviścakāra ||12|| (130)
body.translated_text: <s>Prema</s> (divine love) — a wondrous reality that enters the path of hearing — whose name's glory does anyone truly know? Who has entered into the great sweetness of the forests of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>? Who indeed knows <s>Rādhā</s>, the ultimate limit of sweetness that is the wonder of the highest <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic rapture)? <s>Caitanya-candra</s> (the moon-like Caitanya) alone, through supreme compassion, has revealed everything. ||12|| (130)

body.text:
namaś caitanya-candrāya koṭi-candrānana-tviṣe |
premānandābdhi-candrāya cāru-candrāṃśu-hāsine ||13|| (8)
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Caitanya-candra</s>, whose radiance is that of ten million moons, who is the moon of the ocean of bliss of <s>prema</s> (divine love), who smiles with beautiful moonbeams. ||13|| (8)

body.text:
yasyaiva pādāmbuja-bhakti-labhyaḥ
pramābhidhānaḥ paramaḥ pumarthaḥ |
tasmai jagan-maṅgala-maṅgalāya
caitanya-candrāya namo namas te ||14|| (9)
body.translated_text: To Him, by devotion to whose lotus feet the supreme goal of human life called <s>prema</s> (divine love) is attained, to Him who is the auspiciousness of the world's auspiciousness, to <s>Caitanya-candra</s> — homage, homage to you! ||14|| (9)

body.text:
dadhan mūrdhany ūrdhvaṃ mukulita-karāmbhoja-yugalaṃ
galan-netrāmbhobhiḥ snapita-mṛdu-gaṇḍa-sthala-yugam |
dukūlenāvītaṃ nava-kamala-kiñjalka-rucinā
paraṃ jyotir gauraṃ kanaka-rucira-cauraṃ praṇamata ||15|| (81)
body.translated_text: Bow down to that supreme golden radiance — with both lotus-hands folded above upon the head, with both soft cheeks bathed by tears flowing from the eyes, clad in a garment with the luster of fresh lotus filaments — that stealer of golden beauty. ||15|| (81)

body.text:
siṃha-skandhaṃ madhura-madhuraṃ smera-gaṇḍa-sthalāntaṃ
durvijñeyojjvala-rasa-mayāścarya-nānā-vikāram |
bibhrat kāntiṃ vikaca-kanakāmbhoja-garbhābhirāmām
ekībhūtaṃ vapur avatu vo rādhayā mādhavasya ||16|| (13)
body.translated_text: May the form of <s>Mādhava</s> (Kṛṣṇa) united with <s>Rādhā</s> protect you — with lion-like shoulders, most exceedingly sweet, with smiling cheeks, displaying wondrous and various transformations of brilliant <s>rasa</s> that are hard to comprehend, bearing a splendor as charming as the interior of a fully-bloomed golden lotus. ||16|| (13)

body.text:
pūrṇa-prema-rasāmṛtābdhi-laharī-lolāṅga-gaura-cchaṭā-
koṭy-ācchādita-viśvam īśvara-vidhi-vyāsādibhiḥ saṃstutam |
durlakṣyāṃ śruti-koṭibhiḥ prakaṭayan mūrtiṃ jagan-mohinīm
āścaryaṃ lavaṇoda-rodhasi paraṃ brahma svayaṃ nṛtyati ||17|| (131)
body.translated_text: A golden radiance whose waves from the ocean of the nectar of perfect <s>prema-rasa</s> (the aesthetic rapture of divine love) playfully cover the entire universe with billions of rays, praised by <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s> and others, revealing a form that enchants the world and is imperceptible even to billions of <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) — wonder of wonders, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> Itself dances on the shore of the salt ocean! ||17|| (131)

body.text:
uddāma-dāmanaka-dāma-gaṇābhirāma-
mārāmarāmam avirāma-gṛhīta-nāmā |
kāruṇya-dhāma kanakojjvala-gaura-dhāma
caitanya-nāma paramaṃ kalayāma dhāma ||18|| (69)
body.translated_text: Delightful with garlands of wild <s>dāmanaka</s> flowers, whose beauty enchants even the beautiful garden of <s>Kāmadeva</s>, who ceaselessly chants the Divine Name, the abode of compassion, the golden radiant abode — let us meditate upon that supreme abode named <s>Caitanya</s>. ||18|| (69)

body.text:
avatīrṇe gaura-candre vistīrṇe prema-sāgare |
suprakāśita-ratnaughe yo dīno dīna eva saḥ ||19|| (34)
body.translated_text: When <s>Gaura-candra</s> (the golden moon) has descended and the ocean of <s>prema</s> (divine love) has expanded, with its wealth of jewels brilliantly displayed — whoever remains wretched is truly wretched indeed. ||19|| (34)

body.text:
śravaṇa-manana-saṅkīrtyādi-bhaktyā murārer
yadi parama-pumarthaṃ sādhayet ko'pi bhadram |
mama tu parama-pāra-prema-pīyūṣa-sindhoḥ
kim api rasa-rahasyaṃ dhāma gauraṃ namasyam ||20|| (58)
body.translated_text: If someone were to achieve the supreme goal of human life through devotion to <s>Murāri</s> (Kṛṣṇa) by hearing, contemplation, <s>saṅkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting), and other [practices] — well and good. But for me, the golden abode (<s>Gaura dhāma</s>), which is some mysterious essence of the ocean of the nectar of supreme, transcendent <s>prema</s>, is worthy of my worship. ||20|| (58)

body.text:
niṣṭhāṃ prāptā vyavahṛti-tatir laukikī vaidikī yā
yā vā lajjā prahasan-samudgāna-nāṭyotsaveṣu |
ye vābhuvann ahaha sahaja-prāṇa-dehārtha-dharmā
gauraś cauraḥ sakalam aharat ko'pi me tīvra-vīryaḥ ||21|| (60)
body.translated_text: Whatever worldly or Vedic conventions had reached their established conclusion, whatever modesty [I had] in the festivals of dancing, bursting with laughter and rising up, whatever were my natural life, body, wealth, and duties — that thief <s>Gaura</s>, of exceedingly fierce power, has stolen everything from me! ||21|| (60)

body.text:
mahākarma-sroto-nipatitam api sthairyam ayate
mahā-pāṣāṇebhyo'py atikaṭhinam eti drava-daśām |
naṭaty ūrdhvaṃ niḥsādhanam api mahā-yogi-manasāṃ
bhuvi śrī-caitanye'vatarati manaś citra-vibhave ||22|| (112)
body.translated_text: Even that which has fallen into the torrent of great <s>karma</s> (accumulated actions) becomes steady; even that which is harder than great boulders reaches a state of melting; even the minds of great <s>yogīs</s>, which cannot be raised by any means, dance upward — when Śrī <s>Caitanya</s> of wondrous splendor descends upon the earth. ||22|| (112)

body.text:
strī-putrādi-kathāṃ jahur viṣayiṇaḥ śāstra-pravādaṃ budhā
yogīndrā vijahur marun-niyama-ja-kleśaṃ tapas tāpasāḥ |
jñānābhyāsa-vidhiṃ jahuś ca yatayaś caitanya-candre parām
āviṣkurvati bhakti-yoga-padavīṃ naivānya āsīd rasaḥ ||23|| (113)
body.translated_text: Worldly people abandoned talk of wives and children, the learned abandoned disputation over scriptures, the greatest <s>yogīs</s> abandoned the hardship born of breath-control (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>), ascetics abandoned their austerities, and renunciants abandoned the discipline of cultivating <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) — when <s>Caitanya-candra</s> revealed the supreme path of <s>bhakti-yoga</s> (devotional union), there was no other <s>rasa</s> (taste). ||23|| (113)

body.text:
bhrāntaṃ yatra munīśvarair api purā yasmin kṣamā-maṇḍale
kasyāpi praviveśa naiva dhiṣaṇā yad veda no vā śukaḥ |
yatra kvāpi kṛpāmayena ca nije'py udghāṭitaṃ śauriṇā
tasminn ujjvala-bhakti-vartmani sukhaṃ khelanti gaura-priyāḥ ||24|| (18)
body.translated_text: Where even the greatest sages had wandered in error, into which no one's intellect had ever entered on this earth, which neither the <s>Vedas</s> nor <s>Śuka</s> truly knew, and which <s>Śauri</s> (Kṛṣṇa) Himself, out of compassion, had not revealed even in His own [manifestation] — on that radiant path of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), the beloveds of <s>Gaura</s> sport joyfully. ||24|| (18)

body.text:
īśaṃ bhajantu puruṣārtha-catuṣṭayāśā
dāsā bhavantu ca vidhāya harer upāsāḥ |
kiñcid rahasya-pada-lobhita-dhīr ahaṃ tu
caitanya-candra-caraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ karomi ||25|| (59)
body.translated_text: Let those who desire the four goals of human life worship the Lord; let them become servants by performing worship of <s>Hari</s>. But I, whose mind is captivated by some mysterious state, take refuge at the feet of <s>Caitanya-candra</s>. ||25|| (59)

body.text:
apy agaṇya-mahā-puṇyam ananya-śaraṇaṃ hareḥ |
anupāsita-caitanyam adhanyaṃ manyate matiḥ ||26|| (31)
body.translated_text: Even one possessing immeasurable great merit, who has no other refuge than <s>Hari</s> — if he has not worshipped <s>Caitanya</s>, my understanding considers him unfortunate. ||26|| (31)

body.text:
bhrātaḥ kīrtaya nāma gokula-pater uddāma-nāmāvalīṃ
yad vā bhāvaya tasya divya-madhuraṃ rūpaṃ jagan-mohanam |
hanta prema-mahā-rasojjvala-pade nāśāpi te sambhavet
śrī-caitanya-mahāprabhor yadi kṛpā-dṛṣṭiḥ paten na tvayi ||27|| (82)
body.translated_text: O brother! Chant the abundant garland of names of the Lord of <s>Gokula</s>, or meditate upon His divine, sweet, world-enchanting form. Alas, you cannot even hope to reach the radiant state of the great <s>rasa</s> of <s>prema</s> (divine love) if the merciful glance of Śrī <s>Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s> does not fall upon you. ||27|| (82)

body.text:
bhūto vā bhavitāpi vā bhavati vā kasyāpi yaḥ ko'pi vā
sambandho bhagavat-padāmbuja-rase nāsmin jagan-maṇḍale |
tat sarvaṃ nija-bhakti-rūpa-paramaiśvaryeṇa vikrīḍato
gaurasyaiva kṛpā-vijṛmbhitatayā jānanti nirmatsarāḥ ||28|| (28)
body.translated_text: Whoever has been, will be, or is — whoever they may be — whatever connection they have with the nectar of the lotus feet of the Lord in this worldly sphere, the envy-free ones understand all of that as the manifestation of the mercy of <s>Gaura</s> alone, who sports through the supreme majesty in the form of his own <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). (28)

body.text:
svādaṃ svādaṃ madhurima-bharaṃ svīya-nāmāvalīnāṃ
mādaṃ mādaṃ kim api vivaśībhūta-visrasta-gātraḥ |
vāraṃ vāraṃ vraja-pati-guṇān gāya gāyeti jalpan
gauro dṛṣṭaḥ sakṛd api na yair durghaṭā teṣu bhaktiḥ ||29|| (38)
body.translated_text: Tasting again and again the abundance of sweetness of his own garlands of names, becoming intoxicated beyond control, his limbs loosened with helplessness, calling out "Sing! Sing the qualities of the Lord of <s>Vraja</s>!" — for those who have not seen such <s>Gaura</s> even once, <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) is difficult to attain for them. (29)

body.text:
abhūd gehe gehe tumula-hari-saṅkīrtana-ravo
babhau dehe dehe vipula-pulakāśru-vyatikaraḥ |
api snehe snehe parama-madhurotkarṣa-padavī
davīyasyāmnāyād api jagati gaure'vatarati ||30|| (114)
body.translated_text: In every home arose the tumultuous sound of <s>Hari-saṅkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting of Hari's names); on every body appeared profuse goosebumps mixed with tears; in every affection arose the supreme pinnacle of the most sweet excellence — far beyond even the Vedas — when <s>Gaura</s> descended into the world. (30)

body.text:
jāḍyaṃ karmasu kutracij japa-tapo-yogādikaṃ kutracid-
govindārcana-vikriyā kvacid api jñānābhimānaḥ kvacit |
śrī-bhaktiḥ kvacid ujjvalāpi ca harer vāṅ-mātra eva sthitā
hā caitanya kuto gato'si padavī kutrāpi te nekṣyate ||31|| (138)
body.translated_text: Somewhere there is inertia in duties, somewhere <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>yoga</s>, and the like; somewhere there is elaborate worship of <s>Govinda</s>, somewhere there is pride of knowledge; somewhere the radiant <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) to <s>Hari</s> remains merely in words — Alas, O <s>Caitanya</s>, where have you gone? Your path is nowhere to be seen. (31)

body.text:
vinā bījaṃ kiṃ nāṅkura-jananam andho'pi na kathaṃ
prapaśyen no paṅgur giri-śikharam ārohati katham |
yadi śrī-caitanye hari-rasa-mayāścarya-vibhave'
py abhaktānāṃ bhāvī katham api para-prema-rabhasaḥ ||32|| (39)
body.translated_text: Without a seed, how can a sprout be born? How can a blind man see? How can a lame man climb a mountain peak? Even if <s>Śrī Caitanya</s> possesses the wondrous splendor filled with <s>Hari</s>'s <s>rasa</s> (divine essence), how can the impetuosity of supreme <s>prema</s> (love) arise in non-devotees? (32)

body.text:
akasmād evaitad bhuvanam abhitaḥ plāvitam abhūn
mahā-premāmbhodheḥ kim api rasa-vanyābhir akhilam |
akasmāc cādṛṣṭa-śruta-cara-vikārair alam abhūc
camatkāraḥ kṛṣṇe kanaka-rucirāṅge'vatarati ||33|| (115)
body.translated_text: Suddenly this entire world was flooded everywhere with inexplicable torrents of <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) from the great ocean of <s>prema</s> (divine love); suddenly there arose wondrous amazement with unprecedented and unheard-of extraordinary transformations — when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> descended in a form resplendent as gold. (33)

body.text:
are mūḍhā gūḍhāṃ vicinuta harer bhakti-padavīṃ
davīyasyā dṛṣṭyāpy aparicita-pūrvāṃ munivaraiḥ |
na viśrambhaś citte yadi yadi ca daurlabhyam iva tat
parityajyāśeṣaṃ vrajata śaraṇaṃ gaura-caraṇam ||34|| (80)
body.translated_text: O fools! Search for the hidden path of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) to <s>Hari</s>, that which even the greatest sages have never before seen, even from afar; if there is no confidence in the heart, if it seems unattainable, then abandon everything and take refuge at the feet of <s>Gaura</s>. (34)

body.text:
tāvad brahma-kathā vimukta-padavī tāvan na tiktī-bhavet
tāvac cāpi viśṛṅkhalatvam ayate no loka-veda-sthitiḥ |
tāvac chāstra-vidāṃ mithaḥ kala-kalo nānā-bahir-vartmasu
śrī-caitanya-padāmbuja-priya-jano yāvan na dig-gocaraḥ ||35|| (19)
body.translated_text: Discussions of <s>Brahman</s> and the path of liberation do not become distasteful, worldly and Vedic conventions do not lose their grip, and scholars continue to quarrel among themselves on various external paths — so long as a person dear to the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Caitanya</s> does not come into view. (35)

body.text:
sadā raṅge nīlācala-śikhara-śṛṅge vilasato
harer eva bhrājan-mukha-kamala-bhṛṅgekṣaṇa-yugam |
samuttuṅga-premonmada-rasa-taraṅgaṃ mṛga-dṛśām
anaṅgaṃ gaurāṅgaṃ smaratu gata-saṅgaṃ mama manaḥ ||36|| (70)
body.translated_text: Always sporting joyfully on the peak of <s>Nīlācala</s> (the Blue Mountain), with a pair of bee-like eyes fixed upon the shining lotus face of <s>Hari</s>, with towering waves of the <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) of supreme love-intoxication — may my mind, free from attachment, remember that bodiless <s>Gaurāṅga</s> (golden-limbed one), the delight of doe-eyed women. (36)

body.text:
kvacit kṛṣṇāveśān naṭati bahubhaṅgīm abhinayan
kvacid rādhāviṣṭo hari hari harīty ārta-ruditaḥ |
kvacid riṅgan bālaḥ kvacid api ca gopāla-carito
jagad gauro vismāpayati bahu-bhaṅgī-madhurimā ||37|| (128)
body.translated_text: Sometimes dancing with many gestures, enacting roles through possession by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; sometimes possessed by <s>Rādhā</s>, crying out in anguish "<s>Hari</s>! <s>Hari</s>! <s>Hari</s>!"; sometimes crawling as a child, sometimes enacting the deeds of the cowherd — <s>Gaura</s>, with the sweetness of his many moods, astonishes the world. (37)

body.text:
aye na kuru sāhasaṃ tava hasanti sarvodyamaṃ
janāḥ parita unmadā hari-rasāmṛtāsvādinaḥ |
idaṃ tu nibhṛtaṃ śṛṇu praṇaya-vastu prastūyate
yad eva nigameṣu tat patir ayaṃ hi gauraḥ param ||38|| (83)
body.translated_text: O do not be rash! People everywhere, intoxicated by tasting the nectar of <s>Hari</s>'s <s>rasa</s> (divine essence), laugh at all your efforts. But listen to this secretly — a matter of <s>praṇaya</s> (divine love) is being spoken of: what is in the <s>Nigamas</s> (Vedas), this <s>Gaura</s> is indeed that supreme Lord. (38)

body.text:
udgṛhṇanti samasta-śāstram abhito durvāra-garvāyitā
dhanyaṃ-manya-dhiyaś ca karma-tapa-ādy-uccāvaceṣu sthitāḥ |
dvitrāṇy eva japanti kecana harer nāmāni vāmāśayāḥ
pūrvaṃ samprati gauracandra udite premāpi sādhāraṇaḥ ||39|| (116)
body.translated_text: Some grasp all scriptures thoroughly and swell with irresistible pride; others, considering themselves fortunate, are engaged in high and low practices of <s>karma</s> (ritual action), <s>tapas</s> (austerity), and the like; some with crooked minds chant but two or three names of <s>Hari</s> — but now that the moon of <s>Gaura</s> has risen, even <s>prema</s> (divine love) has become common. (39)

body.text:
pāpīyān api hīna-jātir api duḥśīlo'pi duṣkarmaṇāṃ
sīmāpi śvapacādhamo'pi satataṃ durvāsanāḍhyo'pi ca |
durdeśa-prabhavo'pi tatra vihitāvāso'pi duḥsaṅgato
naṣṭo'py uddhṛta eva yena kṛpayā taṃ gauram eva stumaḥ ||40|| (78)
body.translated_text: Even a sinner, even one of low birth, even one of bad character, even one at the extreme of wicked deeds, even one lower than a <s>śvapaca</s> (outcaste), even one always filled with evil tendencies, even one born in a wretched land, even one residing there, even one in bad company, even one who is lost — is indeed uplifted by his mercy. We praise that <s>Gaura</s> alone. (40)

body.text:
acaitanyam idaṃ viśvaṃ yadi caitanyam īśvaram |
na viduḥ sarva-śāstra-jñā hy api bhrāmyanti te janāḥ ||41|| (37)
body.translated_text: This world is without consciousness (<s>acaitanya</s>); if they do not know <s>Caitanya</s>, the Lord — even those who know all the scriptures, such people wander in delusion. (41)

body.text:
deve caitanya-nāmany avatarati sura-prārthya-pādābja-seve
viṣvadrīcīḥ pravistārayati sumadhura-prema-pīyūṣa-vīcīḥ |
ko bālaḥ kaś ca vṛddhaḥ ka iha jaḍa-matiḥ ko budhaḥ ko varākaḥ
sarveṣām aikarasyaṃ kim api hari-pade bhakti-bhājāṃ babhūva ||42|| (117)
body.translated_text: When the Lord (<s>Deva</s>) descends bearing the name <s>Caitanya</s>, whose lotus feet are worthy of supplication by the gods, spreading in all directions the waves of supremely sweet nectar of divine love (<s>prema</s>) — who is young, who is old, who here is dull-witted, who is learned, who is wretched? A certain indescribable oneness of taste arose for all who partake of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) at the feet of <s>Hari</s>. [42]

body.text:
dattvā yaḥ kam api prasādam atha sambhāṣya smita-śrī-mukhaṃ
dūrāt snigdha-dṛśā nirīkṣya ca mahā-premotsavaṃ yacchati |
yeṣāṃ hanta kutarka-karkaśa-dhiyāṃ tatrāpi nātyādaraḥ
sākṣāt pūrṇa-rasāvatāriṇi harau duṣṭā amī kevalam ||43|| (45)
body.translated_text: He who, by bestowing some grace, or by speaking with a beautiful smiling face, or by gazing from afar with affectionate eyes, grants a great festival of divine love (<s>prema</s>) — alas, for those whose intellects are hardened by sophistry (<s>kutarka</s>), even in His presence there is no great regard. Before <s>Hari</s>, who is the direct descent of the fullness of divine <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic rapture), these people are simply wicked. [43]

body.text:
kāśī-vāsān api na gaṇaye kiṃ gayāṃ mārgaye'haṃ
muktiḥ śuktībhavati yadi me kaḥ parārtha-prasaṅgaḥ |
trāsābhāsaḥ sphurati na mahā-raurave'pi kva bhītiḥ
strī-putrādau yadi kṛpayate deva-devaḥ sa gauraḥ ||44|| (99)
body.translated_text: I do not count even residence in <s>Kāśī</s> — why should I seek <s>Gayā</s>? If liberation (<s>mukti</s>) becomes like a mere shell to me, what concern have I with other goals? Not even a semblance of fear arises, nor is there any terror even in the great <s>Raurava</s> hell — if that golden (<s>Gaura</s>) Lord of lords shows mercy upon my wife, children, and the rest. [44]

body.text:
belāyāṃ lavaṇodadher madhurima-prāg-bhāva-sāra-sphural-
līlāyāṃ nava-vallavī-rasa-nidher āveśayantī jagat |
khelāyām api śaiśave nija-rucā viśvaika-saṃmohinī
mūrtiḥ kācana kāñcana-drava-mayī cittāya me rocate ||45|| (129)
body.translated_text: A certain golden-hued form, shining on the shore of the salt ocean, radiant with the essence of sweetness that preceded [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s] <s>līlā</s> (divine play), immersing the world in the treasure of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic delight) of the new cowherd maidens (<s>vallavī</s>), enchanting the entire universe by its own splendor even in its childhood play — that form delights my heart. [45]

body.text:
dṛṣṭvā mādyati nūtanāmbuda-cayaṃ saṃvīkṣya barhaṃ bhaved
atyantaṃ vikalo vilokya valitāṃ guñjāvalīṃ vepate |
dṛṣṭe śyāma-kiśorake'pi cakitaṃ dhatte camatkāritām
itthaṃ gaura-tanuḥ pracārita-nija-premā hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||46|| (14)
body.translated_text: Seeing a mass of fresh clouds, He becomes intoxicated; beholding a peacock feather, He becomes utterly overwhelmed; upon seeing a twisted garland of <s>guñjā</s> berries, He trembles; and even at the sight of a dark youth, He displays startled wonder — thus may <s>Hari</s>, whose body is golden (<s>Gaura</s>), who has spread abroad His own divine love (<s>prema</s>), protect you! [46]

body.text:
duṣkarma-koṭi-niratasya duranta-ghora-
durvāsanā-nigaḍa-śṛṅkhalitasya gāḍham |
kliśyan mateḥ kumati-koṭi-kadarthitasya
gauraṃ vinādya mama ko bhaviteha bandhuḥ ||47|| (51)
body.translated_text: For one engrossed in tens of millions of sinful deeds, tightly bound by the chains and fetters of terrible and endless evil tendencies (<s>durvāsanā</s>), deeply afflicted in mind, tormented by tens of millions of wicked thoughts — who other than the golden Lord (<s>Gaura</s>) could now be my friend in this world? [47]

body.text:
hā hanta citta-bhuvi me paramoṣarāyāṃ
sad-bhakti-kalpa-latikāṅkuritā kathaṃ syāt |
hṛdy ekam eva paramāśasatnīyam asti
caitanya-nāma kalayan na kadāpi śocyaḥ ||48|| (53)
body.translated_text: Alas! How can the tender shoot of the wish-fulfilling creeper of true devotion (<s>sad-bhakti-kalpa-latikā</s>) sprout in the utterly barren soil of my heart? Yet there is one supremely hopeful thing in my heart: one who contemplates the name <s>Caitanya</s> is never to be pitied. [48]

body.text:
kṛpā-sindhuḥ sandhyāruṇa-rucira-citrāmbara-daro-
jjvalaḥ pūrṇa-premāmṛta-maya-mahājyotir amalaḥ |
śacī-garbha-kṣīrābmbudhibhava udārādbhuta-kalaḥ
kalānāthaḥ śrīmān udayatu mama svānta-nabhasi ||49|| (15)
body.translated_text: May the ocean of mercy, resplendent with beautiful garments colored like the twilight glow, blazing with the great radiance full of the nectar of complete divine love (<s>prema</s>), immaculate, born from the milk-ocean of <s>Śacī</s>'s womb, possessing marvelous and sublime beauty (<s>kalā</s>) — may that glorious Lord of all arts (<s>Kalānātha</s>) rise upon the sky of my inner self. [49]

body.text:
kva tāvad vairāgyaṃ kva ca viṣaya-vārtāsu narake-
ṣvivodvegaḥ kvāsau vinaya-bhara-mādhurya-laharī |
kva tat tejo vālaukikam atha mahā-bhakti-padavī
kva sā vā sambhāvyā yad avakalitaṃ gaura-gatiṣu ||50|| (20)
body.translated_text: Where is detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>)? Where is that alarm regarding sense-objects as though they were hells? Where is that wave of sweetness laden with humility (<s>vinaya</s>)? Where is that otherworldly brilliance, and the path of great devotion (<s>mahā-bhakti</s>) — where is that even conceivable, which is perceived in the ways of the golden Lord (<s>Gaura</s>)? [50]

body.text:
sva-pādāmbhojaika-praṇaya-laharī-sādhana-bhṛtāṃ
śiva-brahmādīnām api ca sumahā-vismaya-bhṛtām |
mahā-premāveśāt kim api naṭanām unmada iva
prabhur gauro jīyāt prakaṭa-paramāścarya-mahimā ||51|| (102)
body.translated_text: May the glorious Lord <s>Gaura</s>, of manifestly supreme and wondrous majesty, be victorious — He who, in a great surge of divine love (<s>mahā-prema</s>), dances in some indescribable manner like one maddened, causing great astonishment even to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the others who bear the flood of exclusive love for His lotus feet. [51]

body.text:
sarve nārada-śaṅkarādaya ihāyātāḥ svayaṃ śrīr api
prāptā deva-halāyudho'pi milito jātāś ca te vṛṣṇayaḥ |
bhūyaḥ kiṃ vraja-vāsino'pi prakaṭā gopāla-gopyādayaḥ
pūrṇa-prema-raseśvare'vatarati śrī-gauracandre bhuvi ||52|| (118)
body.translated_text: All have come here — <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and the rest; <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune) Herself has arrived; Lord <s>Halāyudha</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) too has appeared; the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> also have been born. Moreover, the residents of <s>Vraja</s> too are manifest — <s>Gopāla</s>, the <s>Gopīs</s>, and the rest — now that <s>Śrī Gauracandra</s>, the Lord of the full nectar of divine love (<s>prema-rasa</s>), has descended upon the earth. [52]

body.text:
bhṛtyāḥ snigdhā atha sumadhura-projjvalodāra-bhājas
tat-pādābja-dvitaya-savidhe sarva evāvatīrṇāḥ |
prāpuḥ pūrvādhikatara-mahāprema-pīyūṣa-lakṣmīṃ
sva-premāṇaṃ vitarati jagaty adbhutaṃ hema-gaure ||53|| (119)
body.translated_text: The affectionate servants, possessing supremely sweet, radiant, and noble dispositions, have all descended near His twin lotus feet; they have attained the splendor of the great nectar of divine love (<s>prema</s>) even greater than before — wondrous indeed, when the golden Lord (<s>Hema-Gaura</s>) distributes His own love to the world. [53]

body.text:
alaukikyā premonmada-rasa-vilāsa-prathanayā
na yaḥ śrī-govindānucara-saciveṣv eṣu kṛtiṣu |
mahāścaryaṃ premotsavam api haḍhād dātari na yan
matir gaure sākṣāt para iha sa mūḍho nara-paśuḥ ||54|| (40)
body.translated_text: He who has no regard for these accomplished companions and ministers of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, with their display of unworldly <s>rasa</s> (rapture) of love-madness, and who has no mind toward the golden Lord (<s>Gaura</s>) who readily bestows the wondrous festival of divine love — such a person is verily a deluded beast among men (<s>nara-paśu</s>). [54]

body.text:
asaṅkhyāḥ śruty-ādau bhagavad-avatārā nigaditāḥ
prabhāvaṃ kaḥ sambhāvayatu param īśād itarataḥ |
kim anyat mat-preṣṭhe kati kati satāṃ nāpy anubhavās
tathāpi śrī-gaure hari hari na mūḍhā hari-dhiyaḥ ||55|| (41)
body.translated_text: Innumerable incarnations (<s>avatāra</s>) of the Lord are spoken of in the <s>Śruti</s> and other scriptures. Who can estimate the supreme glory of any except the Lord Himself? What more can I say — even the experiences of the many saints are not sufficient. And yet, alas, alas, regarding <s>Śrī Gaura</s>, the deluded ones do not turn their minds to <s>Hari</s>! [55]

body.text:
rakṣo-daitya-kulaṃ hataṃ kiyad idaṃ yogādi-vartma-kriyā-
mārgo vā prakaṭī-kṛtaḥ kiyad idaṃ sṛṣṭy-ādikaṃ vā kiyat |
mediny-uddharaṇādikaṃ kiyad idaṃ premojjvalāyā mahā-
bhakter vartma-karīṃ parāṃ bhagavataś caitanya-mūrtiṃ stumaḥ ||56|| (7)
body.translated_text: What great feat is this slaying of the clans of <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>Daityas</s>? Or what [significance has] the revelation of the path of <s>yoga</s> and other practices? Or what [is remarkable about] creation and the like? Or what [great deed is] the lifting of the earth and such? We praise the supreme form of the Lord as <s>Caitanya</s>, who established the path of great <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) blazing with divine love (<s>prema</s>). (56)

body.text:
sākṣān-mokṣādikārthān vividha-vikṛtibhis tucchatāṃ darśantaṃ
premānandaṃ prasūte sakala-tanu-bhṛtāṃ yasya līlā-kaṭākṣaḥ |
nāsau vedeṣu gūḍho jagati yadi bhaved īśvaro gauracandras
tat-prāpto'nīśa-vādaḥ śiva śiva gahane viṣṇu-māye namaste ||57|| (42)
body.translated_text: He whose playful sidelong glance produces the bliss of divine love (<s>premānanda</s>) for all embodied beings, showing through various transformations the insignificance of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) and other goals directly — if this Lord <s>Gauracandra</s>, hidden in the <s>Vedas</s>, were not present in the world, then the doctrine of godlessness would have prevailed. O <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>! In [this] profound <s>Viṣṇu-māyā</s>, salutations to you! (57)

body.text:
vāso me varam astu ghora-dahana-vyālāvalī-pañjare
śrī-caitanya-padāravinda-vimukhair mā kutracit saṅgamaḥ |
vaikuṇṭhādi-padaṃ svayaṃ ca militaṃ no me mano lipsate
pādāmbhoja-rasa-cchaṭā yadi manāk gaurasya no rasyate ||58|| (65)
body.translated_text: Let my dwelling be rather in a cage of terrible fire and serpent-rows — but let there never be any association with those who have turned away from the lotus feet of Śrī <s>Caitanya</s>. Even the abode of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and similar realms, offered of their own accord, my mind does not desire to obtain, if the splendor of the nectar of <s>Gaura</s>'s lotus feet is not even slightly tasted. (58)

body.text:
sakṛn nayana-gocarīkṛta-tad-aśru-dhārākula-
praphulla-kamalekṣaṇa-praṇaya-kātara-śrī-mukhaḥ |
na gaura-caraṇaṃ jihāsati kadāpi lokottara-
sphuran-madhurimārṇavaṃ nava-navānurāgonmadaḥ ||59|| (21)
body.translated_text: Once having beheld him, with lotus-eyes blooming wide, tearful streams flowing, his beautiful face tender with affection — one intoxicated with ever-fresh love (<s>anurāga</s>) never wishes to abandon the feet of <s>Gaura</s>, [which are] an ocean of extraordinary, radiant sweetness. (59)

body.text:
ācarya dharmaṃ paricarya viṣṇuṃ
vicarya tīrthāni vicārya vedān |
vinā na gaura-priya-pāda-sevāṃ
vedādi-duṣprāpa-padaṃ vidanti ||60|| (22)
body.translated_text: By practicing <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), by worshiping <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by visiting sacred sites (<s>tīrtha</s>), by studying the <s>Vedas</s> — without the service of the beloved feet of <s>Gaura</s>, they do not attain the state that is difficult to reach even through the <s>Vedas</s> and other [scriptures]. (60)

body.text:
jñānādi-vartma-viruciṃ vraja-nātha-bhakti-
rītiṃ na vedmi na ca sad-guravo milanti |
hā hanta hanta mama kaḥ śaraṇaṃ nigūḍha-
gauro haris tava na karṇa-pathaṃ gato'sti ||61|| (84)
body.translated_text: I have no taste for the path of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and the like; I do not know the way of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) to the Lord of <s>Vraja</s>; nor do I meet true <s>gurus</s> (teachers). Alas, alas, alas! Who is my refuge? O hidden <s>Gaura</s>, O <s>Hari</s>, have you not reached the path of my ears [i.e., have I not heard of you]? (61)

body.text:
mṛgyāpi sā śiva-śukoddhava-nāradādyair
āścarya-bhakti-padavī na davīyastī naḥ |
durbodha-vaibhava-pate mayi pāmare'pi
caitanya-candra yadi te karuṇā-kaṭākṣaḥ ||62|| (55)
body.translated_text: That wondrous path of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), sought even by <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, <s>Uddhava</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and others, is not far from us — O Lord of incomprehensible glory, O <s>Caitanyacandra</s>, if upon me, a wretched one, your compassionate glance [falls]. (62)

body.text:
vṛthāveśaṃ karmasv apanayata vārtām api manāk
na karṇābhyarṇe'pi kvacana nayatādhyātma-saraṇeḥ |
na mohaṃ dehādau bhajata paramāścarya-madhuraḥ
pumarthānāṃ maulir milati bhavatāṃ gaura-kṛpayā ||63|| (85)
body.translated_text: Put aside your futile attachment to rituals; do not bring even a word of the path of <s>adhyātma</s> (spiritual philosophy) near your ears; do not be deluded about the body and such — the supremely wonderful and sweet crest-jewel of all human goals (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) is attained through the grace of <s>Gaura</s>. (63)

body.text:
alaṃ śāstrābhyāsair alam ahaha tīrthāṭanikayā
sadā yoṣid-vyāghryās trasata vitathaṃ thūtkuruta re |
tṛṇaṃ-manyā dhanyāḥy śrayata kila sannyāsi-kapaṭaṃ
naṭantaṃ gaurāṅgaṃ nija-rasa-madād ambudhi-taṭe ||64|| (86)
body.translated_text: Enough of studying the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures)! Enough, alas, of pilgrimage! Always be fearful of women, those tigresses! Spit upon falsehood! Considering [wealth] as straw, O blessed ones, take up the guise of <s>sannyāsa</s> (renunciation) — [and behold] <s>Gaurāṅga</s> dancing on the shore of the ocean, intoxicated by the nectar of his own <s>rasa</s> (divine sentiment)! (64)

body.text:
uccair āsphālayantaṃ kara-caraṇam aho hema-daṇḍa-prakāṇḍau
bāhū proddhṛtya sat-tāṇḍava-tarala-tanuṃ puṇḍarīkāyatākṣam |
viśvasyāmaṅgalaghnaṃ kim api hari-harīty unmadānanda-nādair
vande taṃ deva-cūḍāmaṇim atula-rasāviṣṭa-caitanya-candram ||65|| (10)
body.translated_text: Loudly clapping hands and feet — ah! — raising both arms like golden staffs, his body trembling and unsteady in ecstatic <s>tāṇḍava</s> (cosmic dance), his eyes wide like lotus petals, destroying all inauspiciousness of the universe, with cries of '<s>Hari</s>! <s>Hari</s>!' in intoxicated bliss — I worship that crest-jewel of the gods, <s>Caitanyacandra</s>, overwhelmed by incomparable <s>rasa</s> (divine sentiment). (65)

body.text:
huṅkārair daśa-diṅmukhaṃ mukharayann aṭṭahāsa-cchaṭā-
vīcībhiḥ sphuṭa-kundakairava-gaṇa-prodbhāsi kurvan nabhaḥ |
sarvāṅgaḥ pavanoccalac-cala-dala-prāya-prakampaṃ dadhan
mattaḥ prema-rasonmadāpluta-gatir gauro hariḥ śobhate ||66|| (106)
body.translated_text: Making the ten directions resound with roars, making the sky blaze with waves of bursting laughter like clusters of blooming jasmine and night-lilies, all his limbs quaking as if leaves blown by the wind, intoxicated, his gait immersed in the ecstasy of <s>prema-rasa</s> (the nectar of divine love) — <s>Gaura Hari</s> shines resplendent! (66)

body.text:
kva sā niraṅkuśa-kṛpā kva tad-vaibhavam adbhutam |
kva sā vatsalatā śaure yādṛk gaure tavātmani ||67|| (56)
body.translated_text: Where is that unbridled compassion? Where is that wondrous majesty? Where is that parental affection, O <s>Śauri</s> (descendant of Śūra), such as [is found] in you, O <s>Gaura</s>? (67)

body.text:
ānanda-līlā-maya-vigrahāya
hemābha-divya-cchavi-sundarāya |
tasmai mahā-prema-rasa-pradāya
caitanya-candrāya namo namas te ||68|| (11)
body.translated_text: To him whose form is made of blissful play (<s>ānanda-līlā</s>), who is beautiful with a divine golden (<s>hemābha</s>) splendor, to that bestower of the nectar of great divine love (<s>mahā-prema-rasa</s>) — to <s>Caitanyacandra</s>, salutations again and again! (68)

body.text:
mahā-puruṣa-mānināṃ sura-munīśvarāṇāṃ nijaṃ
padāmbujam ajānatāṃ kim api garva-nirvāsanam |
aho nayana-gocaraṃ nigama-cakra-cūḍā-cayaṃ
śacī-sutam acīkarat ka iha bhūri-bhāgyodayaḥ ||69|| (29)
body.translated_text: Oh, what a supreme arising of fortune — [<s>Caitanya</s>] brought within the sight of eyes the crown and crest of the entire circle of scriptures (<s>nigama</s>), which humbles the pride of great souls, gods, and lords of sages who do not know his own lotus feet, dispelling their ineffable arrogance! The son of <s>Śacī</s> made [this] visible. (69)

body.text:
āstāṃ nāma mahān mahān iti ravaḥ sarva-kṣamā-maṇḍale
loke vā prakaṭāstu nāma mahatī siddhiś camatkāriṇī |
kāmaṃ cāru-caturbhujatvam ayatām ārādhya viśveśvaraṃ
ceto me bahumanyate nahi nahi śrī-gaura-bhaktiṃ vinā ||70|| (66)
body.translated_text: Let there be, if one will, the cry of 'Great! Great!' throughout the entire earth; or let extraordinary, wonder-working <s>siddhi</s> (mystic power) become manifest in the world; let one even attain the beautiful four-armed form by worshiping the Lord of the universe — my heart esteems nothing, nothing at all, without devotion to Śrī <s>Gaura</s>. (70)

body.text:
nirdoṣaś cāru-nṛtyo vidhuta-malinatā-vakra-bhāvaḥ kadācin
niḥśeṣa-prāṇi-tāpa-traya-haraṇa-mahā-prema-pīyūṣa-varṣī |
udbhūtaḥ ko'pi bhāgyodaya-rucira-śacīgarbha-dugdhāmbu-rāśer
bhaktānāṃ hṛc-cakora-svadita-pada-rucir bhāti gaurāṅga-candraḥ ||71|| (107)
body.translated_text: Faultless, dancing beautifully, having dispelled the crooked nature of impurity, showering the great nectar of <s>prema</s> (divine love) that removes the threefold suffering of all beings — arisen like some wondrous moon from the beautiful milk-ocean of the womb of <s>Śacī</s> through the rising of good fortune — <s>Gaurāṅga-candra</s> shines, whose foot-radiance delights the <s>cakora</s> birds that are the hearts of devotees. ||71|| (107)

body.text:
devā dundubhi-vādanaṃ vidadhire gandharva-mukhyā jaguḥ
siddhāḥ santata-puṣpa-vṛṣṭibhir imāṃ pṛthvīṃ samācchādayan |
divya-stotra-parā maharṣi-nivahāḥ prītyopatasthur nija-
premonmādini tāṇḍavaṃ racayati śrī-gauracandre bhuvi ||72|| (133)
body.translated_text: The gods played kettledrums, the chief <s>Gandharvas</s> sang, the <s>Siddhas</s> covered this earth with continuous showers of flowers, hosts of great sages devoted to divine hymns attended with love — when <s>Śrī Gauracandra</s> performed his <s>tāṇḍava</s> (ecstatic dance) on earth, intoxicated with his own <s>prema</s>. ||72|| (133)

body.text:
matta-keśari-kiśora-vikramaḥ
prema-sindhu-jagad-āplavodyamaḥ |
ko'pi divya-nava-hema-kandalī-
komalo jayati gaura-candramāḥ ||73|| (100)
alaṅkāraḥ paṅkeruha-nayana-niḥsyandi-payasāṃ
pṛṣadbhiḥ san-muktā-phala-sulalitair yasya vapuṣi |
udañcad-romāñcair api ca paramā yasya suṣamā
tam ālambe gauraṃ harim aruṇa-rociṣṇu-vasanam ||74|| (71)
body.translated_text: With the prowess of a young intoxicated lion, endeavoring to flood the world with the ocean of <s>prema</s> — some ineffable divine one, tender as a fresh golden plantain, the moon of <s>Gaura</s>, is ever victorious! ||73|| (100) His body is ornamented with dewdrops of tears flowing from lotus eyes, resembling beautiful genuine pearls, and whose supreme beauty also arises from the rising of goose-bumps — I take shelter of that golden <s>Hari</s> wearing garments of reddish luster. ||74|| (71)

body.text:
kandarpād api sundaraḥ surasarit-pūrād aho pāvanaḥ
śītāṃśor api śītalaḥ sumadhuro mādhvīka-sārād api |
dātā kalpa-mahīruhād api mahān snigdho jananyā api
premṇā gaura-hariḥ kadā nu hṛdi me dhyātuḥ padaḥ dhāsyati ||75|| (72)
body.translated_text: More beautiful than <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), more purifying than the flood of the celestial river, cooler than the cool-rayed moon, sweeter than the essence of honey, a greater giver than the wish-fulfilling tree, more affectionate than even a mother — when will <s>Gaura-Hari</s> bestow His feet in the heart of me who meditates upon Him? ||75|| (72)

body.text:
puñjaṃ puñjaṃ madhura-madhur-prema-mādhvī-rasānāṃ
dattvā dattvā svayam urudayo modayan viśvam etat |
eko devaḥ kaṭi-taṭa-milan-mañju-māñjiṣṭa-vāsā
bhāsā nirbhartsita-nava-taḍit-koṭir eva priyo me ||76|| (73)
body.translated_text: Bestowing heap upon heap of the nectar-like <s>rasa</s> of sweet, sweet <s>prema</s>, again and again, the supremely magnanimous one Himself delights this entire universe — that one Lord, clad in a beautiful crimson garment meeting at the waist, whose radiance puts to shame millions of fresh lightning bolts — He alone is dear to me. ||76|| (73)

body.text:
dṛṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ kīrtitaḥ saṃsmṛto vā
dūrasthair apy ānato vādṛto vā |
premṇaḥ sāraṃ dātum īśo ya ekaḥ
śrī-caitanyaṃ naumi devaṃ dayālum ||77|| (4)
body.translated_text: Seen, touched, glorified, remembered, or even bowed to or honored from afar — He who alone is capable of bestowing the essence of <s>prema</s> — I praise that compassionate Lord <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>. ||77|| (4)

body.text:
siñcan siñcan nayana-payasā pāṇḍu-gaṇḍa-sthalāntaṃ
muñcan muñcan pratimuhur aho dīrgha-niḥśvāsa-jātam |
uccaiḥ krandan karuṇa-karuṇo dīrgha-hā-heti-nādo
gauraḥ ko'pi vraja-virahiṇī-bhāva-magnaś cakāsti ||78|| (108)
body.translated_text: Sprinkling, sprinkling the pale surface of his cheeks with tears from his eyes, releasing, releasing repeatedly long-drawn sighs — crying aloud with pitifully piteous sounds of "Hā! Hā!" — some ineffable golden one shines, immersed in the mood of a <s>Vraja</s> woman in separation. ||78|| (108)

body.text:
kiṃ tāvad bata durgameṣu viphalaṃ yogādi-mārgeṣv aho
bhaktiṃ kṛṣṇa-padāmbuje vidadhataḥ sarvārtham āluṇṭhataḥ |
āśā prema-mahotsave yadi śiva-brahmādy-alabhye'dbhute
gaure dhāmani durvigāha-mahimodāre tadā rajyatām ||79|| (87)
body.translated_text: Why indeed toil fruitlessly on the difficult paths of <s>yoga</s> and such? For one who performs <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) to the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> plunders all goals. If there is hope for the great festival of <s>prema</s> — that wondrous state unattainable even by <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> and others — then let one delight in <s>Gaura</s>, the abode of unfathomable and magnanimous glory! ||79|| (87)

body.text:
hasanty uccair uccair ahaha kula-vadhvo'pi parito
dravībhāvaṃ gacchanty api kuviṣaya-grāva-ghaṭitāḥ |
tiraskurvanty ajñā api sakala-śāstrajña-samitiṃ
kṣitau śrī-caitanye'dbhuta-mahima-sāre'vatarati ||80|| (120)
body.translated_text: Even respectable family women laugh loudly all around, even those composed of the stone of vile sense objects melt, even the ignorant surpass the assembly of all scripture-knowers — when <s>Śrī Caitanya</s> of wondrous essential glory descends upon the earth. ||80|| (120)

body.text:
prāyaś caitanyam āsīd api sakala-vidāṃ neha pūrvaṃ yad eṣāṃ
khaarvā sarvārtha-sāre'py akṛta nahi padaṃ kuṇṭhitā buddhi-vṛttiḥ |
gambhīrodāra-bhāvojjvala-rasa-madhura-prema-bhakti-praveśaḥ
keṣāṃ nāsīd idānīṃ jagati karuṇayā gaura-candre'vatīrṇe ||81|| (121)
body.translated_text: Although awareness was mostly present even before among all the learned, their intellectual faculty, being blunted, did not take even a step toward the essence of all goals. But now, when <s>Gaura-candra</s> has descended upon the world through compassion, for whom has there not been entry into the deep, magnanimous, brilliant, sweet <s>prema-bhakti</s> (devotion through divine love) of <s>rasa</s>? ||81|| (121)

body.text:
abhivyakto yatra druta-kanaka-gauro harir abhūn
mahimnā tasyaiva praṇaya-rasa-magnaṃ jagad abhūt |
abhūd uccair uccais tumula-hari-saṅkīrtana-vidhiḥ
sa kālaḥ kiṃ bhūyo'py ahaha parivartate madhuraḥ ||82|| (139)
body.translated_text: Where the golden <s>Hari</s> manifested with the luster of molten gold, by His glory alone the world became immersed in the <s>rasa</s> of <s>praṇaya</s> (intimate love); the tumultuous practice of <s>Hari-saṅkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting) arose higher and higher — alas, will that sweet time ever return again? ||82|| (139)

body.text:
saiveyaṃ bhuvi dhanya-gauḍa-nagarī velāpi saivāmbudheḥ
so'yaṃ śrī-puruṣottamo madhupates tāny eva nāmāni ca |
no kutrāpi nirīkṣyate hari hari premotsavas tādṛśo
hā caitanya kṛpā-nidhāna tava kiṃ vikṣe punar vaibhavam ||83|| (140)
body.translated_text: This is the same blessed city of <s>Gauḍa</s> on earth, this is the same shore of the ocean, this is the same <s>Śrī Puruṣottama</s> (<s>Jagannātha Purī</s>), and these are the same names of <s>Madhupati</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). But nowhere is to be seen, O <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>, such a festival of <s>prema</s>! Alas, O <s>Caitanya</s>, O treasury of mercy, shall I ever again behold Your glory? ||83|| (140)

body.text:
apārāvāraṃ cedam ṛtamaya-pāthodhim adhikaṃ
vimathya prāptaṃ syāt kim api paramaṃ sāram atulam |
tathāpi śrī-gaurākṛti-madana-gopāla-caraṇa-
cchaṭā-spṛṣṭānāṃ tad vahati vikaṭām eva kaṭutām ||84|| (23)
body.translated_text: Even if one were to greatly churn this shoreless ocean of truth and obtain some supreme, incomparable essence, yet for those who have been touched by the ray of the feet of <s>Śrī Gaura</s> in the form of <s>Madana-gopāla</s>, even that bears only an exceedingly bitter taste. ||84|| (23)

body.text:
tṛṇād api sunīcatā sahaja-saumya-mugdhākṛtiḥ
sudhā-madhura-bhāṣitā viṣaya-gandha-thūthūtkṛtiḥ |
hari-praṇaya-vihvalā kim api dhīranārambhitā
bhavanti kila sad-guṇā jagati gaura-bhājām amī ||85|| (24)
body.translated_text: Humility lower than a blade of grass, a naturally gentle and innocent appearance, speech sweet as nectar, utter rejection of even the scent of sense objects, overwhelming emotion in love for <s>Hari</s>, and a certain courageous undertaking — these indeed are the good qualities found in the world among the devotees of <s>Gaura</s>. ||85|| (24)

body.text:
kadā śaure gaure vapuṣi parama-prema-rasade
sad-eka-prāṇe niṣkapaṭa-kṛta-bhāvo'smi bhavitā |
kadā vā tasyālaukika-sad-anumānena mama hṛdy
akasmāt śrī-rādhā-pada-nakha-maṇi-jyotir udabhūt ||86|| (68)
body.translated_text: When shall I have unfeigned devotion toward the golden (<s>Gaura</s>) form of <s>Śauri</s> (Kṛṣṇa), the bestower of supreme <s>prema-rasa</s> (the rapture of divine love), who is truly my sole life? When, by some extraordinary spiritual inference of that [Lord], shall the jewel-light of Śrī <s>Rādhā's</s> toenails suddenly arise in my heart? ||86|| (68)

body.text:
aśrūṇāṃ kim api pravāha-nivahaiḥ kṣauṇīṃ puraḥ paṅkilī-
kurvan pāṇi-tale nidhāya badarī-pāṇḍuṃ kapola-sthalīm |
āścaryaṃ lavaṇoda-rodhasi vasan śoṇaṃ dadhāno'ṃśukaṃ
gaurībhūya hariḥ svayaṃ vitanute rādhā-padābje ratim ||87|| (135)
body.translated_text: Making the earth muddy before him with floods of indescribable streams of tears, placing upon his palm his cheek pale as a jujube fruit — wonder of wonders, dwelling on the shore of the salt ocean, wearing a crimson garment, <s>Hari</s> Himself, having become golden (<s>Gaurībhūya</s>), expands His love for <s>Rādhā's</s> lotus feet. ||87|| (135)

body.text:
sāndrānandojjvala-nava-rasa-prema-pīyūṣa-sindhoḥ
koṭiṃ varṣan kim api kaaurṇa-snigdha-netrāñcalena |
ko'yaṃ devaḥ kanaka-kadalī-garbha-gaurāṅga-yaṣṭiś
ceto'kasmān mama nija-pade gāḍham uptaṃ cakāra ||88|| (61)
body.translated_text: Who is this deity, raining billions [of blessings] from the ocean of the nectar of <s>prema</s> (divine love) brilliant with intense bliss and fresh <s>rasa</s>, with a certain compassionately tender glance from the corner of his eye, with a golden body like the core of a golden plantain tree — who has suddenly planted my mind deeply at His own feet? ||88|| (61)

body.text:
yathā yathā gaura-padāravinde
vindeta bhaktiṃ kṛta-puṇya-rāśiḥ |
tathā tathotsarpati hṛdy akasmāt
rādhā-padāmbhoja-sudhāṃśu-rāśiḥ ||89|| (88)
body.translated_text: To the extent that one of accumulated merit finds devotion at the lotus feet of <s>Gaura</s>, to that very extent there suddenly surges up in the heart the nectar-moon radiance of <s>Rādhā's</s> lotus feet. ||89|| (88)

body.text:
ko'yaṃ paṭṭa-ghaṭī-virājita-kaṭī-deśaḥ kare kaṅkaṇaṃ
hāraṃ vakṣasi kuṇḍalaṃ śravaṇayor bibhrat pade nūpurau |
ūrdhvīkṛtya nibaddha-kuntala-bhara-protphulla-mallī-sragā-
pīḍaḥ krīḍati gaura-nāgara-varo nṛtyan nijair nāmabhiḥ ||90|| (132)
body.translated_text: Who is this, with waist adorned by a silken sash, wearing a bracelet on his hand, a necklace on his chest, earrings on his ears, and anklets on his feet, with upswept bound tresses of hair adorned by a garland of blooming <s>mallī</s> (jasmine) flowers — the best of golden lovers (<s>Gaura-nāgara</s>) sports, dancing to his own names! ||90|| (132)

body.text:
saṃsāra-duḥkha-jaladhau patitasya kāma-
krodhādi-nakra-makaraiḥ kavalīkṛtasya |
durvāsanā-nigaḍitasya nirāśrayasya
caitanya-candra mama dehi padāvalambam ||91|| (54)
body.translated_text: O <s>Caitanya-candra</s>, for me who has fallen into the ocean of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), who is being devoured by the crocodiles and sea-monsters of desire, anger, and the rest, who is shackled by evil tendencies, who has no refuge — grant me the support of your feet! ||91|| (54)

body.text:
kāntyā nindita-koṭi-koṭi-madanaḥ śrīman-mukhendu-cchaṭā-
vicchāyīkṛta-koṭi-koṭi-śarad-unmīlat-tuṣāra-cchaviḥ |
audāryeṇa ca koṭi-koṭi-guṇitaṃ kalpa-drumaṃ hy alpayan
gauro me hṛdi koṭi-koṭi-januṣāṃ bhāgyaiḥ padaṃ dhāsyati ||92|| (74)
body.translated_text: He whose beauty puts to shame billions upon billions of <s>Madanas</s> (Cupids), whose radiance from his beautiful moon-like face makes the luster of billions upon billions of autumn-revealed frost-moons pale in comparison, whose generosity makes even the <s>Kalpa-druma</s> (wish-fulfilling tree) appear trivial when multiplied billions upon billions of times — that <s>Gaura</s> shall place his feet in my heart through the fortune of billions upon billions of births. ||92|| (74)

body.text:
kṣaṇaṃ hasati roditi kṣaṇam atha kṣaṇaṃ mūrcchati
kṣaṇaṃ luṭhati dhāvati kṣaṇam atha kṣaṇaṃ nṛtyati |
kṣaṇaṃ śvasiti muñcati kṣaṇam udāra-hāhā-ravaṃ
mahā-praṇaya-līlayā viharatīha gauro hariḥ ||93|| (134)
body.translated_text: One moment he laughs, the next he weeps; one moment he faints, the next he rolls on the ground and then runs; one moment he dances, the next he breathes heavily and then releases loud cries of "<s>Hā Hā</s>!" — thus <s>Gaura Hari</s> sports here in the play of great divine love. ||93|| (134)

body.text:
kṣaṇaṃ kṣīṇaḥ pīnaḥ kṣaṇam ahaha sāśruḥ kṣaṇam atha
kṣaṇaṃ smeraḥ śītaḥ kṣaṇam anala-taptaḥ kṣaṇaṃ api |
kṣaṇaṃ dhāvan stabdhaḥ kṣaṇam adhika-jalpan kṣaṇam aho
kṣaṇaṃ mūko gauraḥ sphuratu mama deho bhagavataḥ ||94|| (76)
body.translated_text: One moment thin, the next moment full; one moment in tears, alas, the next moment smiling; one moment cold, the next moment burning as if by fire; one moment running, the next standing still; one moment speaking profusely, ah, the next moment mute — may such a form of the Lord <s>Gaura</s> manifest in my body! ||94|| (76)

body.text:
kaivalyaṃ narakāyate tri-daśa-pūr ākāśa-puṣpāyate
durdāntendriya-kāla-sarpa-paṭalī protkhāta-daṃṣṭrāyate |
viśvaṃ pūrṇa-sukhāyate vidhi-mahendrādiś ca kīṭāyate
yat-kāruṇya-kaṭākṣa-vaibhavavatāṃ taṃ gauram eva stumaḥ ||95|| (5)
body.translated_text: <s>Kaivalya</s> (liberation) becomes like hell; the city of the gods becomes like a flower in the sky (an impossibility); the array of untamable sense-serpents of death becomes as if with fangs extracted; the entire world becomes full of perfect bliss; <s>Brahmā</s>, great <s>Indra</s>, and others become like insects — for those who possess the power of His merciful sidelong glance: we praise that <s>Gaura</s> alone. ||95|| (5)

body.text:
pravāhair aśrūṇāṃ nava-jalada-koṭīr iva dṛśor
dadhānaṃ premārdhyā parama-pada-koṭi-prahasanam |
vamantaṃ mādhuryair amṛta-nidhi-koṭīr iva tanū-
cchaṭābhis taṃ vande harim ahaha sannyāsa-kapaṭam ||96|| (12)
body.translated_text: Bearing from his eyes floods of tears like billions of fresh rain-clouds, laughing at billions of supreme abodes through the richness of <s>prema</s> (divine love), pouring forth with his sweetness as if vomiting billions of oceans of nectar through the rays of his body — I bow to that <s>Hari</s>, alas, disguised in the garb of <s>sannyāsa</s> (renunciation)! ||96|| (12)

body.text:
sva-tejasā kṛṣṇa-padāravinde
mahā-rasāveśita-viśvam īśam |
kam apy aśeṣa-śruti-gūḍha-veśaṃ
gaurāṅgam aṅgīkuru mūḍha-cetaḥ ||97|| (57)
body.translated_text: O foolish mind! Embrace <s>Gaurāṅga</s> (the golden-limbed one), the Lord who by his own radiance has immersed the entire world in the great <s>rasa</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> lotus feet, who bears a form hidden from all the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) without exception. ||97|| (57)

body.text:
caitanyeti kṛpāmayeti paramodāreti nānāvidha-
premāveśita-sarva-bhūta-hṛdayety āścarya-dhāmann iti |
gaurāṅgeti guṇārṇaveti rasarūpeti svanāma-priye-
ty āśrāntaṃ mama jalpato janir iyaṃ yāyād iti prārthaye ||98|| (67)
body.translated_text: Calling out "<s>Caitanya</s>!" "The compassionate one!" "The supremely generous one!" "He whose heart has absorbed all beings through various forms of <s>prema</s>!" "The abode of wonders!" "<s>Gaurāṅga</s>!" "Ocean of virtues!" "The embodiment of <s>rasa</s>!" "He who loves his own names!" — ceaselessly thus babbling, I pray that this life of mine may pass away. ||98|| (67)

body.text:
mādyantaḥ paripīya yasya caraṇāmbhoja-sravat-projjvala-
premānanda-mayāmṛtādbhuta-rasān sarve suparveḍitāḥ |
brahmādīṃś ca hasanti nātibahumanyante mahā-vaiṣṇavān
dhik-kurvanti sca jñāna-karma-viduṣas taṃ gauram eva stumaḥ ||99|| (6)
body.translated_text: Those who, becoming intoxicated, have drunk deeply the wondrous nectar of brilliant <s>premānanda</s> (bliss of divine love) flowing from His lotus feet — all of them, supremely nourished, laugh at <s>Brahmā</s> and others, do not greatly esteem even the great <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, and scorn the experts of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>karma</s> (ritual action) — we praise that <s>Gaura</s> alone. ||99||

body.text:
yo mārgo dura-śūnyo ya iha bata balat-kaṇṭako yo'tidurgo
mithyārtha-bhrāmako yaḥ sapadi rasamayānanda-niḥsyandano yaḥ |
sadyaḥ pradyotayaṃs taṃ prakaṭita-mahimā snehavad-dhṛd-guhāyāṃ
ko'py antardhvānta-hantā sa jayati navadvīpa-dīpyat-pradīpaḥ ||100|| (104)
body.translated_text: That path which was remote and desolate, which was forcefully thorny, which was extremely impassable, which led astray with false aims, which now instantly flows with the bliss of <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) — suddenly illuminating it in the cave of the affection-filled heart, some destroyer of inner darkness is victorious: the blazing lamp of <s>Navadvīpa</s>! ||100||

body.text:
dūrād eva dahan kutarka-śalabhān koṭīndu-saṃśītala-
jyotiḥkandala-saṃvalan-madhurimā bāhyāntara-dhvānta-hṛt |
sasnehāśaya-vṛtti-divya-visarat-tejāḥ suvarṇa-dyutiḥ
kāruṇyād iha jājvalīti sa navadvīpa-pradīpo'dbhutaḥ ||101|| (105)
body.translated_text: Burning the moths of sophistry from afar, with the sweetness of light-clusters cool as ten million moons, destroying both outer and inner darkness, with divinely spreading radiance from affection-filled inner dispositions, with a golden luster — out of compassion, that wondrous lamp of <s>Navadvīpa</s> blazes here! ||101||

body.text:
svayaṃ devo yatra druta-kanaka-gauraḥ karuṇayā
mahā-premānandojjvala-rasa-vapuḥ prādurabhavat |
navadvīpe tasmin praibhavana-bhakty-utsava-maye
mano me vaikuṇṭhād api ca madhure dhāmni ramate ||102|| (62)
body.translated_text: Where the Lord Himself, of molten-gold-golden hue, out of compassion, manifested with a body radiant with the brilliant <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) of great <s>premānanda</s> (bliss of divine love) — in that <s>Navadvīpa</s>, full of festivals of devotion to the Lord, my mind delights even more than in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and in the sweet abode (<s>Madhura dhāma</s>). ||102||

body.text:
bibhrad-varṇaṃ kim api dahanottīrṇa-sauvarṇa-sāraṃ
divyākāraṃ kim api kalayan dṛpta-gopāla-mauleḥ |
āviṣkurvan kvacid avasare tat-tad-āścarya-līlāṃ
sākṣād rādhā-madhuripur-vapur bhāti gaurāṅga-candraḥ ||103|| (109)
body.translated_text: Bearing a certain hue surpassing the essence of gold passed through fire, manifesting a certain divine form of the proud cowherd chief, revealing on occasion this or that wondrous <s>līlā</s> (divine play) — as though the very body of <s>Rādhā</s>'s beloved (<s>Madhuripa</s>), <s>Gaurāṅga-candra</s> shines resplendent. ||103||

body.text:
yat tad vadantu śāstrāṇi yat tad vyākhyāntu tārkikāḥ |
jīvanaṃ mama caitanya-pādāmbhoja-sudhaiva tu ||104|| (63)
body.translated_text: Let scriptures say whatever they say, let logicians explain whatever they explain — my life is nothing but the nectar of the lotus feet of <s>Caitanya</s>. ||104||

body.text:
pādāghāta-ravair diśo mukharayan netrāmbhasāṃ veṇībhiḥ
kṣauṇiṃ paṅkilayann aho viśadayann aṭṭāṭṭahāsair nabhaḥ |
candra-jyotir udāra-sundara-kaṭi-vyālola-śoṇāmbaraḥ
ko devo lavaṇoda-kūla-kusumodyāne mudā nṛtyati ||105|| (136)
body.translated_text: Making all directions resound with the stampings of his feet, muddying the earth with streams of tears from his eyes, oh, clearing the sky with great peals of laughter, with a rosy garment swaying at his gracefully broad and beautiful waist, radiant with moonlight — what deity dances joyfully in the flower garden on the shore of the salt ocean? ||105||

body.text:
dhig astu kulam ujjvalaṃ dhig api vāgmitāṃ dhig yaśo
dhig adhyayanam ākṛtiṃ nava-vayaḥ śriyaṃ cāpi dhik |
dvijatvam api dhik para:a vimalam āśramādyaṃ ca dhik
na cet paricitaḥ kalau prakaṭa-gaura-gopī-patiḥ ||106|| (43)
body.translated_text: Fie upon illustrious lineage, fie upon eloquence, fie upon fame, fie upon learning, upon appearance, upon the beauty of youth — fie! Fie even upon being a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, upon the foremost pure <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) — if one has not known the manifest <s>Gaura</s>, Lord of the <s>Gopīs</s>, in the age of <s>Kali</s>. ||106||

body.text:
dhyāyanto giri-kandareṣu bahavo brahmānubhūyāsate
yogābhyāsa-parāś ca santi bahavaḥ siddhā mahī-maṇḍale |
vidyā-śaurya-dhanādibhiś ca bahavo valganti mithyoddhatāḥ
ko vā gaura-kṛpāṃ vinādya jagati premonmado nṛtyatu ||107|| (98)
body.translated_text: Many meditate in mountain caves, experiencing <s>Brahman</s>; many accomplished ones on earth are devoted to the practice of <s>yoga</s>; many boast falsely, puffed up with learning, valor, wealth, and the like — but without the mercy of <s>Gaura</s>, who in this world could dance in the intoxication of <s>prema</s> (divine love)? ||107||

body.text:
antardhvānta-cayaṃ samasta-jagatām unmūlayantī haṭhāt
premānanda-rasāmbudhiṃ niravadhiṃ prodvelayantī balāt |
viśvaṃ śītalayanty atīva vikalaṃ tāpa-trayeṇāniśaṃ
sāsmākaṃ hṛdaye cakāstu satataṃ caitanya-candra-cchaṭā ||108|| (17,75)
body.translated_text: Forcibly uprooting the accumulated inner darkness of all worlds, powerfully causing the boundless ocean of the <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) of <s>premānanda</s> (bliss of divine love) to overflow, cooling the universe exceedingly distressed by the threefold suffering — may that radiance of <s>Caitanya-candra</s> shine forever in our hearts. ||108||

body.text:
upāsatāṃ vā guru-varya-koṭīr
adhīyatāṃ vā śruti-śātra-koṭīḥ |
caitanya-kāruṇya-kaṭākṣa-bhājāṃ
sadyaḥ paraṃ syād dhi rahasya-lābhaḥ ||109|| (25)
body.translated_text: Even if one worships tens of millions of the best of <s>gurus</s>, or studies tens of millions of <s>Śrutis</s> (revealed scriptures) and <s>Śāstras</s> (treatises) — for those who receive the compassionate sidelong glance of <s>Caitanya</s>, the attainment of the supreme secret comes at once. ||109||

body.text:
apārasya premojjvala-rasa-rahasyāmṛta-nidher
nidhānaṃ brahmeśārcita iha hi caitanya-caraṇaḥ |
atas taṃ dhyāyantu praṇaya-bharato yāntu śaraṇaṃ
tam eva pronmattās tam iha kila gāyantu kṛtinaḥ ||110|| (89)
body.translated_text: The feet of <s>Caitanya</s>, worshipped by <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, are the repository of the boundless ocean of the secret nectar of the brilliant <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) of <s>prema</s> (divine love). Therefore, let the blessed ones meditate upon Him with fullness of love, take refuge in Him, and sing of Him here with ecstatic madness. ||110||

body.text:
śrīmad-bhāgavatasya yatra paramaṃ tātparyam uṭṭaṅkitaṃ
śrī-vaiyāsakinā duranvayatayā rāsa-prasaṅge'pi yat |
yad rādhā-rati-keli-nāgara-rasāsvādaika-sad-bhājanaṃ
tad-vastu-prathanāya gaura-vapuṣā loke'vatīrṇo hariḥ ||111|| (122)
body.translated_text: That supreme purport of the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, which was indicated by <s>Śrī Vaiyāsakin</s> (<s>Śuka</s>) even in the context of the <s>Rāsa-līlā</s> (dance of divine love) due to the difficulty of its exposition, that which is the sole worthy vessel for tasting the <s>rasa</s> of the amorous sport of <s>Rādhā</s> and her beloved — for the manifestation of that reality, <s>Hari</s> has descended into the world in a golden form (<s>Gaura</s>). ||111||

body.text:
pātrāpātra-vicāraṇaṃ na kurute na svaṃ paraṃ vīkṣate
deyādeya-vimarśako na hi na vā kāla-pratīkṣaḥ prabhuḥ |
sadyo yaḥ śravaṇekṣaṇa-praṇamana-dhyānādinā durlabhaṃ
datte bhakti-rasaṃ sa eva bhagavān gauraḥ paraṃ me gatiḥ ||112|| (77)
body.translated_text: He does not discriminate between worthy and unworthy recipients, nor does He consider His own versus another's; the Lord does not deliberate on what should or should not be given, nor does He wait for the proper time — He who through hearing, seeing, bowing, meditation, and other means instantly bestows the rarely-attained <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) — that very <s>Bhagavān Gaura</s> is my supreme refuge. ||112||

body.text:
kecid dāsyam avāpur uddhava-mukhāḥ ślāghyaṃ pare lebhire
śrī-dāmādi-padaṃ vrajāmbu-dṛśāṃ bhāvaṃ bhejuḥ pare |
anye dhanyatamā dhayanti madhuraṃ rādhā-rasāmbhonidhiṃ
śrī-caitanya-mahāprabhoḥ karuṇayā lokasya kāḥ sampadaḥ ||113|| (123)
body.translated_text: Some, headed by <s>Uddhava</s>, attained servitude (<s>dāsya</s>); others obtained the praiseworthy status of <s>Śrīdāma</s> and others; still others attained the mood (<s>bhāva</s>) of the doe-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s>; and yet others, the most fortunate, drink deeply of the sweet ocean of <s>Rādhā</s>'s <s>rasa</s> (divine sentiment) — by the mercy of <s>Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s>, what riches has the world [not received]! ||113||

body.text:
sarvajñair muni-puṅgavaiḥ pravitate tat-tan-mate yuktibhiḥ
pūrvaṃ naikataratra ko'pi sudṛḍhaṃ viśvasta āsīj janaḥ |
sampraty apratima-prabhāva udite gaurāṅga-candre punaḥ
śruty-artho hari-bhaktir eva paramaḥ kair vā na nirdhāryate ||114|| (124)
body.translated_text: When previously the omniscient chief sages propounded their various doctrines with reasoning, no one among the people was firmly confident in any single one of them. But now, when the incomparably powerful moon of <s>Gaurāṅga</s> has risen, who does not determine that the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) is that devotion to <s>Hari</s> (<s>hari-bhakti</s>) is the supreme [goal]? ||114||

body.text:
vañcito'smi vañcito'smi vañcito'smi na saṃśayaḥ |
viśvaṃ gaura-rase magnaṃ sparśo'pi mama nābhavat ||115|| (46)
body.translated_text: I have been cheated! I have been cheated! I have been cheated! There is no doubt! The entire world was immersed in the <s>rasa</s> (divine sentiment) of <s>Gaura</s>, yet not even a touch of it came to me! ||115||

body.text:
aho vaikuṇṭha-sthair api ca bhagavat-pārṣada-varaiḥ
saromāñcaṃ dṛṣṭā yad anucara-vakreśvara-mukhāḥ |
mahāścarya-premojjvala-rasa-sadāveśa-vivaśī-
kṛtāṅgās taṃ gauraṃ katham akṛta-puṇyaḥ praṇayatu ||116|| (44)
body.translated_text: Oh, even the foremost attendants of the Lord in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> beheld with goosebumps those [devotees] headed by <s>Vakreśvara</s>, the companion [of <s>Caitanya</s>], whose limbs were rendered helpless by the constant possession of the blazing <s>rasa</s> (divine sentiment) of supremely wondrous love (<s>prema</s>) — how can one devoid of merit love that <s>Gaura</s>? ||116||

body.text:
kair vā sarva-pumartha-maulir akṛtāyāsair ihāsād ito
nāsīd gaura-padāravinda-rajasā spṛṣṭe mahī-maṇḍale |
hā hā dhig mama jīvitaṃ dhig api me vidyāṃ dhig apy āśramaṃ
yad daurbhāgya-bharād aho mama na tad-sambandho-gandho'py abhūt ||117|| (47)
body.translated_text: By whom was the crown of all human goals (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) obtained here without effort, when the circle of the earth was touched by the dust of <s>Gaura</s>'s lotus feet? Alas, alas! Shame upon my life! Shame upon my learning! Shame upon my <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life)! — for, due to the weight of my misfortune, I had not even a trace of connection with Him! ||117||

body.text:
viśvaṃ mahā-praṇaya-sīdhu-sudhā-rasaika-
pāthonidhau sakalam eva nimajjayantam |
gaurāṅga-candra-nakha-candra-maṇi-cchaṭāyāḥ
kañcid vicitram anubhāvam ahaṃ smarāmi ||118|| (125)
body.translated_text: I remember a certain wondrous power of the moonlike radiance from the moon-gem nails of <s>Gaurāṅga-candra</s>, which was submerging the entire universe completely in the ocean consisting solely of the nectar of supremely sweet divine love (<s>praṇaya</s>). ||118||

body.text:
jitaṃ jitaṃ mayādyāpi gaura-smṛty-anubhāvataḥ |
tīrṇāḥ kumata-kāntārāḥ pūrṇāḥ sarva-manorathāḥ ||119|| (?)
body.translated_text: Victory! Victory is mine even now, through the power of remembrance of <s>Gaura</s>! The wilderness of false doctrines has been traversed; all desires of the heart are fulfilled! ||119||

body.text:
dante nidhāya tṛṇakaṃ padayor nipatya
kṛtvā ca kāku-śatam etad ahaṃ bravīmi |
he sādhavaḥ sakalam eva vihāya dūrād
gaurāṅga-candra-caraṇe kurutānurāgam ||120|| (90)
body.translated_text: Placing a blade of grass between my teeth, falling at your feet, and making a hundred entreaties, I say this: O saints (<s>sādhus</s>)! Abandon everything far away and cultivate loving attachment (<s>anurāga</s>) to the feet of <s>Gaurāṅga-candra</s>! ||120||

body.text:
patanti yadi siddhayaḥ karatale svayaṃ durlabhāḥ
svayaṃ ca yadi sevakī-bhavitum āgatāḥ syuḥ surāḥ |
kim anyad idam eva me yadi caturbhujaṃ syād vapus
tathāpi na mano manāk calati gauracandrān mama ||121|| (64)
body.translated_text: Even if rare <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural accomplishments) fall of their own accord into the palm of my hand, even if the gods themselves were to come offering to become servants, and even more — even if this body of mine were to become four-armed — still my mind would not waver in the slightest from <s>Gauracandra</s>. ||121||

body.text:
aho na durlabhā muktir na ca bhaktiḥ sudurlabhā |
gauracandra-prasādas tu vaikuṇṭhe'pi sudurlabhaḥ ||122|| (91)
body.translated_text: Oh, liberation (<s>mukti</s>) is not difficult to obtain, nor is devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) extremely rare; but the grace of <s>Gauracandra</s> is exceedingly rare even in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>! ||122||

body.text:
so'py āścarya-mayaḥ prabhur nayanayor yan nābhavad gocaro
yan nāsvādi hareḥ padāmbuja-rasas tad yad gataṃ tad gatam |
etāvan mama tāvad astu jagatīṃ ye'dyāpy alaṅkurvate
śrī-caitanya-pade nikhāta-manasas tair yat prasaṅgotsavaḥ ||123|| (50)
body.translated_text: That wondrous Lord did not come within the range of my eyes, nor was the <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) of <s>Hari</s>'s lotus feet tasted — what has gone, has gone. Let this much at least be mine for now: a joyful festival of association with those whose minds are firmly fixed at the feet of <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>, who still adorn the world today. ||123||

body.text:
utsasarpa jagad eva pūrayan
gauracandra-karuṇā-mahārṇavaḥ |
bindu-mātram api nāpatan mahā-
durbhage mayi kim etad adbhutam ||124|| (48)
body.translated_text: The great ocean of <s>Gauracandra</s>'s compassion rose up, flooding the entire world; yet not even a single drop fell upon me, greatly unfortunate that I am — is this not astonishing? ||124||

body.text:
kālaḥ kalir balina indriya-vairi-vargāḥ
śrī-bhakti-mārga iha kaṇṭaka-koṭi-ruddhaḥ |
hā hā kva yāmi vikalaḥ kim ahaṃ karomi
caitanya-candra yadi nādya kṛpāṃ karoṣi ||125|| (49)
body.translated_text: The age is <s>Kali</s>; the hosts of sense-enemies are powerful; the path of sacred devotion (<s>śrī-bhakti-mārga</s>) is obstructed here by tens of millions of thorns. Alas, alas! Where shall I go? What shall I, helpless, do — if you, O <s>Caitanya-candra</s>, do not show mercy today? ||125||

body.text:
kalinda-tanayā-taṭe sphurad-amanda-vṛndāvanaṃ
vihāya lavaṇāmbudheḥ pulina-puṣpa-vāṭīṃ gataḥ |
dhṛtāruṇa-paṭaḥ parākṛta-supīta-vāsā haris
tirohita-nija-cchaviḥ prakaṭa-gaurimā me gatiḥ ||126|| (79)
body.translated_text: Having left behind the radiantly delightful <s>Vṛndāvana</s> on the bank of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), He has gone to the flower-garden on the shore of the salt ocean (<s>Purī</s>). Wearing saffron robes, having set aside His beautiful yellow garment, <s>Hari</s>, with His own splendor concealed, manifest in golden radiance (<s>gaurimā</s>) — He is my refuge. ||126||

body.text:
āstāṃ vairāgya-koṭir bhavatu śama-dama-kṣānti-maitry-ādi-koṭis
tattvānudhyāna-koṭir bhavatu bhavatu vā vaiṣṇavī bhakti-koṭiḥ |
koṭy-aṃśo 'py asya na syāt tad api guṇa-gaṇo yaḥ svataḥ-siddha āste
śrīmac-caitanyacandra-priya-caraṇa-nakha-jyotir āmoda-bhājām ||127|| (26)
body.translated_text: Set aside ten million-fold detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>); let there be ten million-fold tranquility, self-control, forbearance, friendliness, and the rest; let there be ten million-fold contemplation of the ultimate reality (<s>tattva</s>); and let there be ten million-fold Vaiṣṇava devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) — even a ten-millionth part of that could not match the aggregate of virtues that exist as self-manifest in those who partake of the fragrance of the radiance from the beloved toenails of <s>Śrīmac Caitanyacandra</s>. ||127||

body.text:
bhajantu caitanya-padāravindaṃ
bhavantu sad-bhakti-rasena pūrṇāḥ |
ānandayantu tri-jagad-vicitra-
mādhurya-saubhāgya-dayā-kṣamādyaiḥ ||128|| (92)
body.translated_text: May they worship the lotus feet of <s>Caitanya</s>; may they be filled with the <s>rasa</s> (divine essence) of true devotion (<s>sad-bhakti</s>); may they delight the three worlds with wondrous sweetness, good fortune, compassion, forbearance, and the rest! ||128||

body.text:
jñāna-vairāgya-bhakty-ādi
sādhayantu yathā tathā |
caitanya-caraṇāmbhoja-
bhakti-labhya-samaṃ kutaḥ ||129|| (94)
body.translated_text: Let them accomplish <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (detachment), <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), and other [practices] however they wish — where can they find anything equal to that which is obtained through devotion to the lotus feet of <s>Caitanya</s>? ||129|| (94)

body.text:
hā hanta hanta paramoṣara-citta-bhūmau
vyarthībhavanti mama sādhana-koṭayo'pi |
sarvātmanā tad aham adbhuta-bhakti-bījaṃ
śrī-gauracandra-caraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ karomi ||130|| (52)
body.translated_text: Alas, alas, alas! In the utterly barren ground of my heart, even billions of spiritual practices become fruitless. Therefore, with my entire being, I take refuge at the feet of Śrī <s>Gauracandra</s>, the wondrous seed of devotion. ||130|| (52)

body.text:
sarva-sādhana-hīno'pi paramāścarya-vaibhave |
gaurāṅge nyasta-bhāvo yaḥ sarvārtha-pūrṇa eva saḥ ||131|| (30)
body.translated_text: Even one devoid of all spiritual practices — if he has placed his heart in <s>Gaurāṅga</s> of supremely wondrous glory, he is indeed one who has fulfilled all purposes. ||131|| (30)

body.text:
brahmeśādi-mahāścarya-mahimāpi mahāprabhuḥ |
mugdha-bāloditaṃ śrutvā snigdho'vaśyaṃ bhaviṣyati ||132|| (142)
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāprabhu</s>, whose glory astonishes even <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva), and others, will certainly become affectionate upon hearing the innocent speech of a child. ||132|| (142)

body.text:
dṛṣṭaṃ na śāstraṃ guravo na pṛṣṭā
vivecitaṃ nāpi budhaiḥ sva-buddhyā |
yathā tathā jalpatu bāla-bhāvāt
tathāpi me gaurahariḥ prasīdatu ||133|| (143)
body.translated_text: I have not studied the scriptures, I have not consulted teachers, I have not analyzed anything through my own intellect with the learned. Let me babble however I may, in childlike innocence — may <s>Gaura Hari</s> still be pleased with me! ||133|| (143)

body.text:
kecit sāgara-bhūdharān api parākrāmanti nṛtyanti vai
kecid deva-purandarādiṣ mahā-kṣepaṃ kṣipante muhuḥ |
ānandodbhaṭa-jāla-vihvalatayā te'dvaita-candrādayaḥ
ke kiṃ no kṛtavanta īdṛśi punaś caitanya-nṛtyotsave ||134|| (27)
body.translated_text: Some surpass even oceans and mountains, some dance indeed, some hurl great insults at <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, and others again and again — <s>Advaita-candra</s> and the others, overwhelmed by the net of overflowing ecstasy — what did they not do in this festival of <s>Caitanya's</s> dance? ||134|| (27)

body.text:
avatīrṇe gauracandre vistīrṇe prema-sāgare |
ye na majjanti majjanti te mahānartha-sāgare ||135|| (35)
body.translated_text: When <s>Gauracandra</s> descended and the ocean of <s>prema</s> expanded, those who do not plunge into it plunge instead into the ocean of great calamity. ||135|| (35)

body.text:
prasārita-mahā-prema-pīyūṣa-rasa-sāgare |
caitanya-candre prakaṭe yo dīno dīna eva saḥ ||136|| (36)
body.translated_text: When <s>Caitanya-candra</s> is manifest, having spread wide the ocean of the nectar of great <s>prema</s> — whoever remains wretched is truly wretched indeed. ||136|| (36)

body.text:
gītā-bhāgavataṃ paṭhatv avirataṃ tīrthāni saṃsevatāṃ
śālagrāma-śilāṃ samarcayatu vā kāla-trayaṃ pratyaham |
muktibhyo mahatīṃ pumān na labhate tat-koṣa-bhūṣāṅkarīṃ
bhaktiṃ premamayīṃ śacīsuta-pada-dvandvānukampāṃ vinā ||137|| (?)
body.translated_text: Let one read the <s>Gītā</s> and <s>Bhāgavata</s> unceasingly, let one visit all the sacred sites (<s>tīrthas</s>), let one worship the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone three times daily — yet a person does not obtain that great devotion filled with <s>prema</s> (divine love), which is the jewel-ornament adorning the treasury of liberations (<s>muktis</s>), without the compassion of the twin feet of the son of <s>Śacī</s>. ||137|| (?)

body.text:
āśā yasya pada-dvandve caitanyasya mahāprabhoḥ |
tasyendro dāsavad bhāti kā kathā nṛpa-kīṭake ||138|| (96)
body.translated_text: He who places his hope at the twin feet of <s>Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s> — before him, even <s>Indra</s> appears like a servant. What need to speak of a petty king? ||138|| (96)

body.text:
yasyāśā kṛṣṇa-caitanye rāja-dvāri kim arthinaḥ |
cintāmaṇi-cayaṃ prāpya ko gūḍho rajataṃ vrajet ||139|| (97)
body.translated_text: For one who has hope in <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, what need is there to petition at royal courts? Having obtained a heap of wish-fulfilling gems (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>), who would foolishly go after silver? ||139|| (97)

body.text:
mādyat-koṭi-mṛgendra-huṅkṛti-ravas tigmāṃśu-koṭi-cchaviḥ
koṭīndūdbhava-śītalo gati-jita-pronmatta-koṭi-dvipaḥ |
nāmnā duṣkṛta-koṭi-niṣkṛti-karo brahmādi-koḍīśvaraḥ
koṭy-advaita-śiromaṇir vijayate śrī-śrī-śacī-nandanaḥ ||140|| (103)
body.translated_text: Whose roar is like the thundering of billions of intoxicated lions, whose splendor is like billions of blazing suns, who is cool like [the light of] billions of moons arising, whose gait surpasses billions of maddened elephants, whose name expiates billions of sins, who is the Lord of billions [ruling] over <s>Brahmā</s> and others, the crest-jewel of billions of <s>Advaitas</s> — victorious is the glorious son of <s>Śacī</s>! ||140|| (103)

body.text:
ati-puṇyair ati-sukṛtaiḥ kṛtārthīkṛtaḥ ko'pi pūrvaiḥ |
evaṃ kair api na kṛtaṃ yat premābdhau nimajjitaṃ viśvam ||141|| (126)
body.translated_text: Someone made fulfilled by exceedingly great merit and exceedingly great virtue from previous [lives] — no one has ever done what he did: the entire world was plunged into the ocean of <s>prema</s>. ||141|| (126)

body.text:
yadi nigadita-mīnādy-aṃśavad gauracandro
na tad api sa hi kaścic chakti-līlā-vikāśaḥ |
atula-sakala-śaktyāścarya-līlā-prakāśair
anadhigata-mahattvaḥ pūrṇa evāvatīrṇaḥ ||142|| (141)
body.translated_text: Even if <s>Gauracandra</s> is spoken of as being like a portion of a fish incarnation (<s>Mīna</s>) and other [avatāras</s>], even that is but some manifestation of his power-play (<s>śakti-līlā</s>). Through the wondrous play of his incomparable, complete powers, his greatness being unattainable [by comparison], he has descended as the Complete One (<s>Pūrṇa</s>) himself. ||142|| (141)

body.text:
saṃsāra-sindhu-taraṇe hṛdayaṃ yadi syāt
saṅkīrtanāmṛta-rase ramate manaś cet |
premāmbudhau viharaṇe yadi citta-vṛttiś
caitanya-candra-caraṇe śaraṇaṃ prayātu ||143|| (93)
acaitanyam idaṃ viśvaṃ yadi caitanyam īśvaram |
bhajet sarvato mṛtyur upāsyam amarottamaiḥ ||??|| (95)
body.translated_text:
If the heart desires to cross the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), if the mind delights in the nectarine <s>rasa</s> of <s>saṅkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting), if the activity of the mind is toward sporting in the ocean of <s>prema</s> (divine love) — let one take refuge at the feet of <s>Caitanya-candra</s>. ||143|| (93)
This world is without consciousness (<s>acaitanya</s>) — if it were to worship <s>Caitanya</s>, the Lord, death would be overcome in every way, [for He is] worshipped by the best of the immortals. ||??|| (95)
